s: Aeneas is a Trojan hero (pious toward the gods)
q: Aeneas, not inferior in the field, In pious reverence to the gods excell’d.

s: Aeneas is a match for Turnus (in single combat)
q: He calls me hand to hand, And I alone will answer his demand.

s: Latinus presides over the council of Latinus (as supreme ruler)
q: Supreme in pow’r, and reverenc’d for his years, He takes the throne, and in the midst appears.

s: Aeneas possesses Aeneas’s lance (a formidable weapon)
q: With what a whirling force his lance he toss’d! Heav’ns! what a spring was in his arm, to throw!

s: Aeneas possesses Aeneas’s shield (a powerful shield)
q: How high he held his shield, and rose at ev’ry blow!

s: Priam is a old
q: As ev’n old Priam might with pity view.

s: Ulysses encounters Charybdis (during his wanderings)
q: Ulysses with his men Have seen Charybdis and the Cyclops’ den.

s: Turnus is a Daunian prince (rival of Drances)
q: Then Drances took the word, who grudg’d, long since, The rising glories of the Daunian prince.

s: Turnus has ambition ambition
q: For whose ambition (let me dare to say, Fear set apart, tho’ death is in my way) The plains of Latium run with blood around.

s: the council of Latinus is a council of the Latins
q: The Latian senate to the council hall.

s: Turnus challenges single combat between Turnus and Aeneas (to protect the public peace)
q: If you consent, he shall not be refus’d, Nor find a hand to victory unus’d. This new Achilles, let him take the field,

s: Turnus is a warrior (willing to fight Aeneas alone)
q: For you, my royal father, and my fame, I, Turnus, not the least of all my name, Devote my soul. He calls me hand to hand, And I alone will answer his demand.

s: Drances opposes Turnus (politically and rhetorically)
q: He rose, and took th’ advantage of the times, To load young Turnus with invidious crimes.

s: Lavinia is a royal bride (whose marriage is proposed as the basis of peace)
q: Give him the fair Lavinia for his bride; With that alliance let the league be tied,

s: Latinus proposes Latin-Trojan peace proposal (to save the Latins and satisfy their foes)
q: You see th’ event.—Now hear what I propose, To save our friends, and satisfy our foes.

s: Latin-Trojan peace proposal offers the common country (the Trojan shall command)
q: Those mountains fill’d with firs, that lower land, If you consent, the Trojan shall command, Call’d into part of what is ours; and there, On terms agreed, the common country share.

s: Latin-Trojan peace proposal includes galleys (twenty or more ships to be built)
q: Then twice ten galleys let us build with speed, Or twice as many more, if more they need.

s: Latin-Trojan peace proposal includes presents (to be sent with the peace delegation)
q: To treat the peace, a hundred senators Shall be commission’d hence with ample pow’rs, With olive the presents they shall bear,

s: Latin princes attend the council of Latinus (at the king’s command)
q: The princes come, commanded by their head, And crowd the paths that to the palace lead.

s: Latinus offers gold (as part of the peace presents)
q: And sums of gold. Among yourselves debate This great affair, and save the sinking state.”

s: Latins are defeated by the Trojans (in the current war)
q: Vanquish’d without resource; laid flat by fate; Factions within, a foe without the gate!

s: Latins possess Latium (including land along the Tiber)
q: A tract of land the Latins have possess’d Along the Tiber, stretching to the west,

s: Rutulians cultivate Latium (along with the Auruncans)
q: Which now Rutulians and Auruncans till, And their mix’d cattle graze the fruitful hill.

s: Auruncans cultivates Latium (along with the Rutulians)
q: Which now Rutulians and Auruncans till, And their mix’d cattle graze the fruitful hill.

s: Messapus supports Latins (as a remaining ally)
q: The great Messapus yet remains our friend:

s: Tolumnius supports Latins (as a prophetic ally)
q: Tolumnius, who foretells events, is ours;

s: Camilla is a Volscian Amazon (leader of an army)
q: Above the rest, the Volscian Amazon Contains an army in herself alone, And heads a squadron, terrible to sight,

s: Italian chiefs and princes support Latins (with their forces)
q: Th’ Italian chiefs and princes join their pow’rs

s: Arcadian troops retires Turnus
q: All saw, but he, th’ Arcadian troops retire In scatter’d squadrons, and their prince expire.

s: Venulus performs your high command
q: When Venulus began, the murmuring sound Was hush’d, and sacred silence reign’d around. “We have,” said he, “perform’d your high command,

s: war is a conflict (between Latins and Trojans)
q: O citizens, we wage unequal war, With men not only Heav’n’s peculiar care,

s: peace treaty is a proposed settlement (offered to end the Latin-Trojan conflict)
q: Make peace, ye Latians, and avoid with care Th’ impending dangers of a fatal war.’

s: the embassy to Diomedes reaches the place desir'd
q: We reach’d the place desir’d; with wonder fill’d, The Grecian tents and rising tow’rs beheld. Great Diomede has compass’d round with walls

s: the embassy to Diomedes requests audience from the king (after presenting gifts)
q: When introduc’d, our presents first we bring, Then crave an instant audience from the king.

s: Diomede has city Argyripa
q: Great Diomede has compass’d round with walls The city, which Argyripa he calls,

s: Diomede calls Argyripa (the city)
q: The city, which Argyripa he calls, From his own Argos nam’d.

s: Aeneas leads the Trojans (in battle)
q: Aeneas draws his forces to the field, And moves his camp.

s: Latinus is a old man (ruler of the Latins)
q: Good old Latinus, when he saw, too late, The gath’ring storm just breaking on the state,

s: Latinus has an easy temper (which he regards as culpable)
q: Dismiss’d the council till a fitter time, And own’d his easy temper as his crime,

s: Latinus complies with the broken treaty (against his reason, for the promised bride)
q: Who, forc’d against his reason, had complied To break the treaty for the promis’d bride.

s: the council of Latinus is dismissed a fitter time
q: Dismiss’d the council till a fitter time,

s: the city has walls (defended against attack)
q: And the fierce foes in arms approach the walls.”

s: the city has a gate (at which the enemy is expected)
q: Break short the pirate’s lance; pronounce his fate, And lay the Phrygian low before the gate.”

s: Latins defend the city (against the Trojans)
q: Where, with the gods, averse, the Latins fight.

s: war is a armed conflict (between the Latins and the Trojans)
q: Meantime Latonian Phoebe, from the skies, Beheld th’ approaching war with hateful eyes,

s: the ambush is located in the mountain pass (a concealed military position)
q: Inclos’d with hills, a winding valley lies, By nature form’d for fraud, and fitted for surprise. A narrow track, by human steps untrode, Leads, thro’ perplexing thorns, to this obscure abode.

s: Camilla is a warrior queen (leader of the Volscians)
q: The Volscians, with their virgin leader, wait His last commands. Then, with a graceful mien, Lights from her lofty steed the warrior queen:

s: the Trojans are descried near the river (marching toward the city)
q: Th’ unpleasing news, the Trojans are descried, In battle marching by the river side, And bending to the town.

s: Camilla is a virgin (devoted to Diana and vowed to chastity)
q: But she disdains their love, to share with me The sylvan shades and vow’d virginity.

s: Camilla promises their defeat
q: If sense of honour, if a soul secure Of inborn worth, that can all tests endure, Can promise aught, or on itself rely Greatly to dare, to conquer or to die; Then, I alone, sustain’d by these, will meet The Tyrrhene troops, and promise their defeat.

s: Camilla opposes Tuscans (in battle)
q: Then, I alone, sustain’d by these, will meet The Tyrrhene troops, and promise their defeat.

s: Camilla is a Amazon (trained as a warrior from childhood)
q: The little Amazon could scarcely go: He loads her with a quiver and a bow;

s: Camilla is daughter of Metabus (rescued and raised by him)
q: Her father Metabus, when forc’d away From old Privernum, for tyrannic sway, Snatch’d up, and sav’d from his prevailing foes, This tender babe, companion of his woes.

s: Camilla is daughter of Casmilla (her mother)
q: Casmilla was her mother; but he drown’d One hissing letter in a softer sound, And call’d Camilla.

s: Diana is a goddess of the woods (patroness of arms and wilderness)
q: ‘Accept, great goddess of the woods,’ he said, ‘Sent by her sire, this dedicated maid! Thro’ air she flies a suppliant to thy shrine;

s: Diana loves Camilla (as her most valued mortal nymph)
q: The nymphs I lov’d of all my mortal train, Invested with Diana’s arms, in vain. Nor is my kindness for the virgin new: ’Twas born with her; and with her years it grew.

s: Diana calls Opis (her most belov'd and ever-trusty maid)
q: And call’d the light-foot Opis to her aid, Her most belov’d and ever-trusty maid;

s: Metabus raises Camilla (in the wilderness)
q: A shepherd’s solitary life he led; His daughter with the milk of mares he fed.

s: Diana avenges Camilla’s death (regardless of whether the slayer is Trojan or Italian)
q: By whate’er hand Camilla shall be slain, Or of the Trojan or Italian train, Let him not pass unpunish’d from the plain.

s: the broken treaty is caused by Latinus (under pressure and against his reason)
q: Who, forc’d against his reason, had complied To break the treaty for the promis’d bride.

s: Turnus uses the ambush (as a military stratagem)
q: With chosen foot his passage to forelay, And place an ambush in the winding way.

s: Turnus occupies the mountain pass (in ambush)
q: Thither young Turnus took the well-known way, Possess’d the pass, and in blind ambush lay.

s: Volusus commands Volscians (under Turnus’s orders)
q: Thou, Volusus, the Volscian troops command To mount; and lead thyself our Ardean band.

s: Messapus posts your force (to charge the Trojan horse)
q: Messapus and Catillus, post your force Along the fields, to charge the Trojan horse.

s: Catillus posts Tuscans (to charge the Trojan horse)
q: Messapus and Catillus, post your force Along the fields, to charge the Trojan horse.

s: Camilla is a warrior (woman warrior and Volscian maid)
q: A woman warrior was too strong for thee.

s: Camilla is a Volscian maid (martial leader)
q: Then Aruns, doom’d to death, his arts assay’d, To murder, unespied, the Volscian maid:

s: Camilla serves Diana (as a votary)
q: Yet unreveng’d thy goddess will not leave Her vot’ry’s death, nor; with vain sorrow grieve.

s: Diana possesses Diana’s arms (sacred arms borne by Camilla)
q: Nor aught avail’d, in this unhappy strife, Diana’s sacred arms, to save thy life.

s: Camilla possesses Diana’s arms (borne on her shoulder)
q: Diana’s arms upon her shoulder sound;

s: Camilla possesses bow and arrow (uses in combat)
q: Now from afar her fatal jav’lins play; Now with her ax’s edge she hews her way: Diana’s arms upon her shoulder sound; And when, too closely press’d, she quits the ground, From her bent bow she sends a backward wound.

s: Camilla is a leader (of the Volscians)
q: Their leader lost, the Volscians quit the field,

s: Camilla’s death is struck by the winged weapon (in her pap)
q: when the jav’lin whizz’d along the skies, Both armies on Camilla turn’d their eyes, Directed by the sound. Of either host, Th’ unhappy virgin, tho’ concern’d the most, Was only deaf; so greedy was she bent On golden spoils, and on her prey intent; Till in her pap the winged weapon stood Infix’d, and deeply drunk the purple blood

s: Camilla’s death is a death (death of Camilla in battle)
q: She said, and, sliding, sunk upon the plain: Dying, her open’d hand forsakes the rein; Short, and more short, she pants; by slow degrees Her mind the passage from her body frees.

s: Aruns is a traitor (concealed attacker)
q: To mark the traitor Aruns from the height.

s: Tarchon is sent to th' abandon’d plain (to redeem)
q: He fires the breast of Tarchon with disdain, And sends him to redeem th’ abandon’d plain.

s: Tarchon commands Tuscan troops (after their retreat)
q: Betwixt the broken ranks the Tuscan rides, And these encourages, and those he chides; Recalls each leader, by his name, from flight; Renews their ardour, and restores the fight.

s: Tarchon captures Venulus (in battle)
q: The first he found he seiz’d with headlong haste, In his strong gripe, and clasp’d around the waist; ’Twas Venulus, whom from his horse he tore,

s: Jupiter is a god (supreme observer of the battle)
q: Now mighty Jove, from his superior height, With his broad eye surveys th’ unequal fight.

s: Apollo grants half his pray’r (shuffled in winds the rest)
q: Apollo heard, and, granting half his pray’r, Shuffled in winds the rest, and toss’d in empty air.

s: Tuscans is a horse (Tuscan force)
q: By this, the Trojan and the Tuscan horse, Drawn up in squadrons, with united force,

s: Phoebus is a god (addressed as patron of Socrates’ high abodes)
q: O patron of Socrates’ high abodes, Phoebus, the ruling pow’r among the gods,

s: Acca receives message from Camilla (Camilla’s final instructions)
q: “Acca, ’tis past! he swims before my sight, Inexorable Death; and claims his right. Bear my last words to Turnus; fly with speed,

s: Turnus is a Daunian (leader of the Latian resistance)
q: Inflam’d with rage, (for so the Furies fire The Daunian’s breast, and so the Fates require,)

s: Turnus is ordered to my charge (repel the Trojans, and the town relieve)
q: Bear my last words to Turnus; fly with speed, And bid him timely to my charge succeed, Repel the Trojans, and the town relieve:

s: Volscians is a troops (under Camilla’s leadership)
q: Their leader lost, the Volscians quit the field,

s: Volscians retreats to Latin city (after Camilla’s death)
q: Confus’d in flight, they bear each other down, And spur their horses headlong to the town.

s: Trojan–Tuscan alliance is a alliance (combined force in the battle)
q: By this, the Trojan and the Tuscan horse, Drawn up in squadrons, with united force,

s: Messapus leads Latian horse (in opposition to the Trojan and Tuscan forces)
q: Oppos’d to these, come on with furious force Messapus, Coras, and the Latian horse;

s: Battle of Camilla ends with night (armies entrenched before the town)
q: Intrench’d before the town both armies lie, While night with sable wings involves the sky.

s: fear and panic relies on their speed (when their captains fly)
q: The frighted soldiers, when their captains fly, More on their speed than on their strength rely.

s: Camilla has band Camilla’s band
q: These in the body plac’d, on either hand Sustain’d and clos’d by fair Camilla’s band.

s: Camilla commands Italian female warriors (in war)
q: Her maids, in martial pomp, on either side, Larina, Tulla, fierce Tarpeia, ride: Italians all; in peace, their queen’s delight; In war, the bold companions of the fight.

s: Turnus is prepared in arms (to combat hand to hand)
q: No more excuses or delays: I stand In arms prepar’d to combat, hand to hand, This base deserter of his native land.

s: Aeneas is struck by a winged arrow (while unmindful of defence)
q: Thus while he spoke, unmindful of defence, A winged arrow struck the pious prince.

s: Aeneas’ wound is a arrow wound (its human or divine source is unknown)
q: But, whether from some human hand it came, Or hostile god, is left unknown by fame: No human hand or hostile god was found, To boast the triumph of so base a wound.

s: Latinus possesses Latin lands and treasures (offered to Turnus)
q: You want not wealth, or a successive throne, Or cities which your arms have made your own: My towns and treasures are at your command,

s: Latinus possesses Latinus’ royal scepter (as a symbol of kingship)
q: Ev’n as this royal scepter” (for he bore A scepter in his hand) “shall never more Shoot out in branches, or renew the birth:

s: Lavinia is a unmarried noblewoman (fair and of noble family)
q: Laurentum more than one Lavinia sees, Unmarried, fair, of noble families.

s: Lavinia is promised to Turnus (as a bride)
q: I promis’d my Lavinia for your bride:

s: Amata is a queen (who fears for Turnus)
q: But now the queen, who fear’d for Turnus’ life, And loath’d the hard conditions of the strife,

s: Turnus challenges single combat between Turnus and Aeneas (to decide the war)
q: Renew the truce; the solemn rites prepare, And to my single virtue trust the war. The Latians unconcern’d shall see the fight; This arm unaided shall assert your right:

s: Juturna is a water nymph (of a neighboring flood)
q: Compress’d by force, but, by the grateful god, Now made the Nais of the neighb’ring flood.

s: Juturna is sister of Turnus (as Turnus’s sister)
q: the goddess of the lake, King Turnus’ sister, once a lovely maid,

s: Juturna assumes Camertus’s appearance (to incite the Rutulians)
q: Dissembling her immortal form, she took Camertus’ mien, his habit, and his look;

s: Juno is a queen of Heaven
q: Meantime the Queen of Heav’n beheld the sight,

s: Juno has lord my wand’ring lord
q: Long hast thou known, nor need I to record, The wanton sallies of my wand’ring lord.

s: Juno supports the Latian side (while fortune favour’d)
q: While fortune favour’d, nor Heav’n’s King denied To lend my succour to the Latian side, I sav’d thy brother, and the sinking state:

s: Jupiter is a god (king of Heaven)
q: Thou, King of Heav’n, and thou, the Queen of Air,

s: Rutulians support Turnus (as their champion)
q: Already the Rutulians deem their man O’ermatch’d in arms, before the fight began.

s: the Trojans issues from the camp (in arms divine)
q: Then issued from the camp, in arms divine, Aeneas, author of the Roman line;

s: Turnus accepts death (if Heaven decrees it)
q: Resolv’d on fight, I am no longer free To shun my death, if Heav’n my death decree.

s: peace treaty requires single combat between Turnus and Aeneas (to settle the quarrel)
q: Our single swords the quarrel shall decide, And to the victor be the beauteous bride.

s: Latins break peace treaty (after the omen and incitement)
q: Peace leaves the violated fields, and hate Both armies urges to their mutual fate.

s: war is joined by the Latine troops
q: The wish’d insult the Latine troops embrace, And meet their ardour in the middle space.

s: divine omen appears as th’ imperial bird of Jove (in the fiery tracts above)
q: For, sudden, in the fiery tracts above, Appears in pomp th’ imperial bird of Jove: A plump of fowl he spies, that swim the lakes,

s: Aeneas proposes equal status to the Italians (in their laws, their lands, and their abodes)
q: My Trojans shall not o’er th’ Italians reign: Both equal, both unconquer’d shall remain, Join’d in their laws, their lands, and their abodes;

s: Turnus stakes the crown and beauteous bride (if my prostrate body press the plain)
q: Then, if my prostrate body press the plain, To him the crown and beauteous bride remain.

s: Turnus wields Turnus’ falchion (in combat)
q: Then to his head his glitt’ring helm he tied, And girt his faithful falchion to his side.

s: Turnus wields Actor’s lance (in preparation for the duel)
q: Propp’d on a pillar, which the ceiling bore, Was plac’d the lance Auruncan Actor wore; Which with such force he brandish’d in his hand,

s: Aeneas is a Trojan leader (founder of the Roman line)
q: Then issued from the camp, in arms divine, Aeneas, author of the Roman line;

s: Aeneas agrees to single combat between Turnus and Aeneas (as the means of deciding the quarrel)
q: The Trojan and Rutulian troops no more Shall dye, with mutual blood, the Latian shore: Our single swords the quarrel shall decide,

s: Aeneas proposes peace treaty (between Trojans and Italians)
q: My Trojans shall not o’er th’ Italians reign: Both equal, both unconquer’d shall remain, Join’d in their laws, their lands, and their abodes;

s: Turnus is a The Prince
q: That flying Turnus still declin’d the fight, The Prince, whose piety had long repell’d

s: Aeneas receives the healing potion (for his wound)
q: The leech, unknowing of superior art Which aids the cure, with this foments the part; And in a moment ceas’d the raging smart.

s: Aeneas’s wounding and healing is a divine healing (wounding followed by miraculous restoration)
q: This is no mortal work, no cure of mine, Nor art’s effect, but done by hands divine.

s: Venus is a goddess (divine mother of Aeneas)
q: But now the goddess mother, mov’d with grief, And pierc’d with pity, hastens her relief.

s: Venus brings dittany (as a healing plant from Crete)
q: A branch of healing dittany she brought, Which in the Cretan fields with care she sought:

s: Venus prepares the healing potion (with ambrosian dews and medicinal herbs)
q: This Venus brings, in clouds involv’d, and brews Th’ extracted liquor with ambrosian dews, And odorous panacee.

s: Juturna is the sister of Turnus (she protects him from Aeneas)
q: Now here, now there, her conqu’ring brother shows; Now with a straight, now with a wheeling flight, She turns, and bends, but shuns the single fight.

s: Juturna assumes the form of Metiscus (to drive Turnus’s chariot)
q: Assumes his shape, his armour, and his mien, And, like Metiscus, in his seat is seen.

s: Latinus is a king (ruler of the Latins)
q: The helpless king is hurried in the throng, And, whate’er tide prevails, is borne along.

s: Turnus is a king (victorious in battle)
q: He lies revers’d; the victor king descends,

s: Amata is a royal woman (ruler’s queen and Lavinia’s mother)
q: And to her dames and to her daughter known,

s: Amata is the mother of Lavinia (her daughter mourns her death)
q: The sad Lavinia rends her yellow hair And rosy cheeks; the rest her sorrow share:

s: Amata commits the queen’s suicide (in despair after believing Turnus dead)
q: Then round a beam a running noose she tied, And, fasten’d by the neck, obscenely died.

s: the queen’s suicide is caused by her anguish (impotent to bear the mighty grief)
q: Mad with her anguish, impotent to bear The mighty grief, she loathes the vital air.

s: the Trojans are led by Aeneas
q: Aeneas leads; and draws a sweeping train, Clos’d in their ranks, and pouring on the plain.

s: Latins view the cover’d plains
q: With him the Latins view’d the cover’d plains, And the chill blood ran backward in their veins.

s: the armies fight each other (in open field)
q: And now both armies shock in open field;

s: war is fought between the Trojans (against the Latins)
q: Jove, could’st thou view, and not avert thy sight, Two jarring nations join’d in cruel fight,

s: war begins at the city (and is destined to end there)
q: There it began, and there the war shall end.

s: Turnus commands the chariot (as its driver in battle)
q: At once his arms and coursers he requires; Then, with a leap, his lofty chariot gains, And with a ready hand assumes the reins.

s: peace treaty is breached by th’ Ausonian prince
q: Attests the gods, asserts his innocence, Upbraids with breach of faith th’ Ausonian prince;

s: the city is a seat of war (and source of the conflict)
q: Your instant arms against the town prepare, The source of mischief, and the seat of war.

s: the city has citizens slain citizens (without the town)
q: Without the town, an unprovided train Of gaping, gazing citizens are slain.

s: Turnus is the brother of Juturna (she is his sister and protects him)
q: She steers a various course among the foes; Now here, now there, her conqu’ring brother shows;

s: Turnus is opposed by Aeneas (in single combat and in war)
q: Aeneas, fir’d with fury, breaks the crowd, And seeks his foe, and calls by name aloud:

s: Aeneas is a Trojan hero (general and prince)
q: The wounded prince is forc’d to leave the field:

s: Aeneas is the father of Ascanius (his son)
q: Thou, when thy riper years shall send thee forth To toils of war, be mindful of my worth; Assert thy birthright, and in arms be known, For Hector’s nephew, and Aeneas’ son.”

s: Aeneas is the son of Venus (divine mother)
q: But now the goddess mother, mov’d with grief, And pierc’d with pity, hastens her relief.

s: Aeneas is wounded and healed by Venus (with divine medicine)
q: This Venus brings, in clouds involv’d, and brews Th’ extracted liquor with ambrosian dews, And odorous panacee.

s: Turnus is a prince (Daunian and Rutulian champion)
q: Thus flies the Daunian prince, and, flying, blames His tardy troops, and, calling by their names,

s: Aeneas carries Aeneas’s shield (a Vulcanian shield)
q: But, vain against the great Vulcanian shield, The mortal-temper’d steel deceiv’d his hand:

s: Aeneas is wounded recently knit wound (the wound retards his pursuit)
q: Aeneas hastens, tho’ with heavier pace— His wound, so newly knit, retards the chase,

s: Juturna sustains the driver’s office
q: She who the driver’s office now sustains,

s: Juturna is sister of Turnus (devoted to saving him)
q: Ah me!” she cries, “in this unequal strife What can thy sister more to save thy life?

s: Juturna is commanded by Juno (to try to save Turnus)
q: ’Tis true, Juturna mingled in the strife By my command, to save her brother’s life,

s: Juturna is forced to bear eternity (Tho’ born to death, not privileg’d to die)
q: Tho’ born to death, not privileg’d to die, But forc’d to bear impos’d eternity!

s: Jupiter is a god (Thund’rer and founder of mankind)
q: Then thus the founder of mankind replies (Unruffled was his front, serene his eyes)

s: Turnus is brother of Juturna
q: Who sent you down from heav’n, involv’d in air, Your share of mortal sorrows to sustain, And see your brother bleeding on the plain?

s: Jupiter is husband of Juno (addresses her as Queen of Heaven)
q: Meantime imperial Jove to Juno spoke, Who from a shining cloud beheld the shock:

s: Jupiter commands Juno (to cease aiding Turnus)
q: Now cease at my command.” The Thund’rer said;

s: Jupiter sends the Fury (against Juturna)
q: One sister plague if these from heav’n he sent, To fright Juturna with a dire portent.

s: Juno requests the peace (when the nuptial bed shall bind it)
q: This let me beg (and this no fates withstand) Both for myself and for your father’s land, That, when the nuptial bed shall bind the peace,

s: Jupiter establishes the peace between Latins and Trojans (with Latin customs and language retained)
q: From ancient blood th’ Ausonian people sprung, Shall keep their name, their habit, and their tongue. The Trojans to their customs shall be tied:

s: Latins retain their name (under the peace settlement)
q: From ancient blood th’ Ausonian people sprung, Shall keep their name, their habit, and their tongue.

s: Latins retain their language (under the peace settlement)
q: From ancient blood th’ Ausonian people sprung, Shall keep their name, their habit, and their tongue.

s: the Trojans retain their customs (under the peace settlement)
q: The Trojans to their customs shall be tied: I will, myself, their common rites provide;

s: Turnus is son of Daunus
q: Pity my sire, now sinking to the grave; And for Anchises’ sake old Daunus save!
